key_idea: Use an auxiliary integer M with many divisors, so that one unit fraction reduces u/(MQ) to a small residue of -Qt mod u; make this work for almost all numerators using exponential-sum equidistribution of prime products and a uniform divisor-moment bound, then reach every numerator by writing a multiple gAM as the sum of two elements of the dense set.
reason: Several ideas here are good: the reduction from a dense family to every numerator by splitting into two summands, the divisor-indexed residue identity, and the short squaring argument for the lower bound. However, the core descent relies on a large apparatus (Kloosterman-type sums over 1/n, random prime products, Hölder recurrences for exceptional sets, divisor moments with shift uniformity) and heavy bookkeeping of constants and levels, so the reason the result holds gets buried under technical control.
